 JUDGMENT The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.75,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
2. That on 05.07.2018 at about 09.15 p.m, petitioner was driving his car bearing No.KA-51-ME- 6259, on Bengaluru-Shivamogga NH-206 road, near Hindiskere Village, Kibbanahalli Hobli, at the same time driver of the Lorry bearing No.KA-13-B-0289 came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's car.
Due to the said impact, petitioner sustained severe head injury.

3. It is further stated that, immediately he was shifted to Tumkur Government Hospital, wherein first aid was given, then he was shifted to Sparsh Hospital, Bangalore, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and again he was admitted to St.John's Medical College hospital, where the petitioner was managed conservatively and discharged on 27.7.2018.

Again he was admitted to Sparsh Hospital on 25.7.2018 and discharged on 18.8.2019. and spent Rs.25,00,000/- towards medicines,
attendant charges, food and nourishment etc.
4.
It is stated that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 53 years and working as a supervisor and earning Rs.23,000/- per month.
After the accident the petitioner is still under coma, under complete bed rest and these accidental injuries suffered permanent disability and sustained loss of income.
5. It is stated that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of lorry bearing registration No.KA-13-B-289.

Due to the accidental injuries petitioner still under coma, the driver of the lorry took the advantage of the situation and lodged a false complaint against the petitioner before Kibbanahalli Police station in Cr.No.76/2018.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are Diwakar.K vs Rafeeq on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113615382/
2 jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

6. In response to issuance of notice, respondents have appeared before the tribunal.
The respondent No.2 & 3 appeared and filed their written statements.
On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has not filed his written statement.

7. In the written statement, the respondent No.2 has contended that, the respondent No.1 was obtained policy, by issuing cheque towards premium amount, but the said cheque was dishonoured,
the policy stood cancelled with immediate effect.
Hence, there was no policy for the lorry bearing No.KA-13-B-289.

Further contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the party of the driver of the car, who came to his extreme right, has rammed into the lorry and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner and also denied the expenses incurred towards medical and other incidental charges.
Ultimately, stated that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, exaggerated and arbitrary.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.

8. Further the respondent No.2 has filed additional written statement and contended that the petitioner himself was driving the car in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the front side of lorry, there is no insurance to the car, the petitioner had no valid and effective driving licence, the driver of the lorry has lodged complaint against the petitioner/driver of the car, in turn the police have filed charge sheet.
There is no negligence on the part of the lorry driver, the police have filed wrong charge sheet against the lorry driver as accused No.2.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition.

9. Further, the respondent No.2 has filed the additional written statement and contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner and not the driver of the lorry.

Further contended that there is no policy in respect of lorry and the premium cheque has been dishonoured and the policy has been cancelled, hence, the petitioner is not entitled to get any compensation from this respondent.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.

10. The respondent No.3 in the written statement, admitted about the issuance of policy in respect of car bearing No.KA-51-ME-6259 and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further contended that at the time of accident the petitioner being the driver of the car bearing No.KA-51-ME-6259 drove the same without having valid and effective driving licence.
The petitioner being the owner he is not a third party and he cannot claim compensation against this respondent.
The tort feasor cannot be a third party and he is not entitled for any compensation u/s 166 of the MV Act.
With all these grounds prays to dismiss the petition.

3 5.7.2018 at about 9.15 p.m. near Hindiskere village, on NH-206 road, Kibbanahalli Hobli, Tumkur?
2.
Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, at what rate and from whom?
3. What order or award?

It is the specific case of the petitioner that due to actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Lorry bearing registration No.KA-13-B-289 the alleged accident had taken place,
consequently he had sustained grievous injuries.

18. On the other hand, the respondent No.2 is the insurer of the lorry bearing No.KA-13-B-289 has contended in its written statement that, accident occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the petitioner.
As per the police documents except the charge sheet there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry.
The police have wrongly filed the charge sheet against the driver of the lorry.
Hence, there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the Lorry.
19. The respondent No.3 is the insurer of the car contended that the petitioner is the tort feasor cannot be a third party and he is not entitled for any compensation.

20. On the basis of rival contention of both the parties, the petitioners have to place satisfactory evidence on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities against both the vehicles in question.
On the other hand, onus shifts on the respondents to prove by means of cogent and convincing evidence.

On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by one Abdul Rahim, the S.H.O. of Thibbanahalli Cross Police have registered the case against the driver of the car bearing No.KA-51-ME- 6259 for the offences punishable under section 279, 337 and 304(A) of IPC.

27. Apart from this, on going through the charge sheet marked at Ex.P6 submitted by the investigation officer against the drivers of both the vehicles for the offences punishable under section 279, 338 and 304(A) of IPC.

Though the police papers are not substantive piece of evidence to consider the claim petition, in the absence of contra materials, there is no hurdle to believe the said document as conclusive proof in connection with the above fact in issue.
28. Added to this, on perusal of the recitals of the police documents, there is clear narration about the involvement of both the vehicles in the accident.

On keen observation of the evidence of PW1 and the documents produced by her, it is clear that, at the first instance police have registered case against the driver of the car only and after investigation charge sheeted against both the drivers.
If the driver of the car should have taken little bit care and caution while driving his vehicle, he would have avoided the accident.
Hence, it is crystal clear that due to the negligence of both the drivers of the offending vehicles the accident occurred, the negligence is distinct.

29. At the time of cross-examination of PW1 admitted that right side of their car and front side of the car caused damages and both the tyres were punctured and also admitted that they have lodged complaint against the driver of the lorry.

ISSUE No.2:
33.This
issue is with respect to the entitlement of reliefs claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition, claiming compensation of Rs.75,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident under different heads.

34. Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by him,
in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injuries cases in Motor Vehicle Act.
Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.
The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.
The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

"while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation.
PW1 has stated in her evidence that, the petitioner has sustained the injuries in a road traffic accident.
In connection with the injuries she has produced discharge summary marked as Ex.P10.

The said document discloses that, the petitioner had sustained the following injuries:-
1) Severe traumatic brain injury, diffuse axonal injury, RIB fractures with left pleural effusion 36. PW1 has produced discharge summaries, MLC extract, neuropsychological assessment report as per Ex.P10 to Ex.P12.

Loss of income during treatment period:
37.With respect to the loss of income during laid up period and rest period is concerned, in the case on hand, on going through the facts and circumstances of the case, nature of the injuries sustained by him and its consequences as per the evidence of the PW1, prima-facie reveal that, after the accident, due to the severe injuries sustained by the petitioner and also due to his critical condition of head injury, he was in coma, has not attended for his job after the accident.
And loss of income in toto occurred to him, after the accident.
As such, while considering the loss of future income each and every aspect to be discussed.
Because there is a total loss of income to him after the accident, till today he is under the medication and had lost his consciousness, he cannot do any work in future.
And also no improvements from his side to do normal life in future, as per the evidence of the PW1.

As such, regard,
compensation under the head of loss of income during the laid up period and rest period has not been considered.

b) Conveyance:
41.
Since the petitioner is not able to move due to the physical disability, it is not possible to take the petitioner in any of public conveyance to the hospital.
Either wife of the petitioner or any attendant who takes care of the petitioner has to engage taxi or ambulance whenever they want to take the petitioner for follow-up treatment.
Hence, it is reasonable to award Rs.1,50,000/- towards past and future conveyance.

c) Atendant Charges;
42.
In the case on hand, it is true that the petitioner has not produced any document to show that one attendant or nurse was engaged to look after the petitioner.
It is also relevant to note that the petitioner requires treatment till his recovery.
It is also to be noted that the petitioner was treated as an inpatient almost 5 months.
Thereafter, he was discharged with the advise of follow-up treatment.
As could be seen from the medical bills placed by the petitioner, the petitioner has taken treatment in various hospitals.

On perusal of the evidence of PW1 and in the cross-examination, it reveals that petitioner is still bed bound, on tracheostomy tube, obeying commands inconsistently, not verbalizing and possibilities are less to improve his condition in future.

9 43.
Having seen the medical documents of the petitioner, it could be said that one attendant was absolutely required for the petitioner atleast for some period.
As stated in the psychological assessment report petitioner is bed bound and completely dependent for all activities, he was not well groomed and needed to be cared for.
He made eye contact intermittently as his posture was stooped and needed much proddding to focus attention.
He tended to drool and had to be reminded to keep his mouth closed and given opinion that "symptom profile and neuropsychological findings are indicative of sever post TBI sequelae".
Therefore, petitioner requires attendant, who though may not be medically trained must be capable to handle the bed ridden petitioner.
Thus, certainly one attendant is absolutely required to take care of the petitioner throughout his life.

Even if it is considered that either the mother or father ore wife of the petitioner might be taking care of the petitioner without appointing the attendant then also they will leave their wages for taking care of the petitioner.
If the minimum wages of a person is considered of Rs.4,000/- per month.

In Kajal's case referred supra the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that multiplier system should be followed not only for determining the compensation on account of loss of income, but also for determining the attendance charges etc.,
The age of the petitioner considered as 53 years, hence, the multiplier applicable to the case on hand is '11'.

If the attendant charges of Rs.4,000/- per month has been considered and the multiplier 11 is applied then the petitioner is entitled to Rs.5,28,000/-
(Rs.4,000/-X12X11)towards attendance charges.
Hence, it is just and proper to award sum of Rs.5,28,000/- towards attendant charges.

Loss of future income;
44.
The PW1 herein, asserting that, petitioner had sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by him.

He had repeated bed sores.

48. In connection with the age of the petitioner is concerned, on going through the cause title of the petition reveals that, as on the date of the petition, his age is 53 years.

49. Next factual aspect of the income of the petitioner is concerned, PW1 in his evidence the petitioner has stated that, prior to the accident, petitioner was working as a supervisor, Power Control Electrical, Bengaluru and earning Rs.22,000/- per month.
He has placed employment certificate and pay slips at Ex.P13 to Ex.P15.

If, future prospects of 10% is taken into consideration, it will comes at Rs.2,584/-.
In toto, the income of the petitioner is at Rs.28,430/- per month.

50. In the light of my detailed discussions held above, no doubt injuries sustained by the petitioner,
definitely come in the way of his future, to do her daily routine work, as well as to do his work for livelihood on going through his age criteria.

Hence, the petitioner herein, is entitled for compensation under loss of future income as follows:
